item.title: The Impact of the Political Environment on Tourism and Hospitality
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks to explore the multifaceted ways in which political environments shape and influence the tourism and hospitality sectors. The political context encompasses governmental policies, political stability, regulatory frameworks, international relations, and geopolitical events that directly and indirectly affect tourism flows, hospitality operations, and industry development.

We invite submissions that examine how political factors influence destination competitiveness, tourism demand and supply, hospitality business strategies, employment patterns, and sustainable development in the sector. We particularly welcome research that addresses contemporary political challenges and opportunities in tourism and hospitality.

Contributions may include empirical studies, theoretical frameworks, case studies, and comparative analyses that provide insights into the complex relationships between political environments and tourism and hospitality industries globally.

Appel publié par Journal of Hospitality & Tourism Research. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

item.title: Responsible and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in Tourism and Hospitality
item.content:encoded:
Brian King, Texas A&M University

Kyoung Jun Lee, Kyung Hee University

Danae Manika, Brunel University of London

Babak Taheri, Texas A&M University

The aim of this special issue is to advance scholarly understanding of Responsible and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in tourism and hospitality, by assembling cutting-edge research, innovative methodologies, and critical reflections. As AI technologies become embedded in-service delivery, marketing, operations, and consumer experience, transformative opportunities are accompanied by potential ethical challenges. Issues of fairness, accountability, transparency, and trust are particularly pressing as the sector adopts AI in pursuit of personalization, efficiency, and engagement. Responsible AI is linked with the concept of "trustworthy AI," which reflects a stronger technological view and focuses on systems that are lawful, ethical, and robust throughout their lifecycle. Earlier research in tourism and hospitality has shown the need for interdisciplinary inquiry regarding the technical, managerial, legal, and societal dimensions of responsible AI adoption.

Appel publié par Electronic Markets. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Ethical AI frameworks in tourism and hospitality: fairness, accountability, transparency, and inclusivity.
  • AI-driven consumer experiences: balancing personalization, convenience, and privacy.
  • AI robustness and risk: testing booking, pricing, and chatbot vulnerabilities, modeling threats, and strengthening resilience.
  • Trust, reliability and safety: building consumer trust, ensuring reliable performance, and managing risks.
  • Auditing AI systems: ongoing evaluations in pursuit of fairness, accuracy, and compliance.
  • Generative AI in marketing: pursuing responsibility in branding, engagement, and consumer journeys.
  • Sociotechnical and cultural dimensions: cross-cultural and historical perspectives on AI adoption.
  • AI, sustainability, and CSR: supporting or hindering responsible and sustainable practices in tourism and hospitality.
  • Future directions: conceptual frameworks and policy challenges for responsible and trustworthy AI in service innovation and resilience.
  • Social and labor impacts: the effects of adopting AI on employment, equity, and workforce well-being.
  • Frugal AI and digital twins: cost-effective and resource-conscious applications for operations and guest experiences.
  • Algorithmic transparency and rights: making AI decisions understandable and offering recourse for affected consumers.
  • Dark side of AI: risks of manipulation, surveillance, over-automation, and addictive design.
  • Corporate digital responsibility (CDR) in the age of AI within tourism and hospitality.
  • AI on digital platforms: exploring recommender systems, marketplaces, and platform governance.
  • Data ecosystems: sharing and leveraging user/usage data across digital travel and hospitality platforms.
  • Trustworthy AI principles: ensuring AI systems in tourism and hospitality are lawful, ethical, and technically robust.
  • Verification, validation, and explainability: designing AI that is interpretable and auditable for multiple stakeholders.
  • Trustworthy AI and consumer journeys: balancing automation with transparency and user empowerment.

Timeline

  • September 15, 2026: Submission deadline

item.title: A Decade (2015-2025) of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): Trends, Reflections, and Realignments in Hospitality and Tourism Research
item.content:encoded:
Edmund Goh, Les Roches Abu Dhabi Hospitality Academy

Jun Wen, Macau University of Science and Technology

Siamak Seyfi, University of Oulu

C. Michael Hall, Massey University

Xin-Jean Lim, Sun Yat-Sen University

September 2025 marked the 10th anniversary of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a global blueprint for achieving peace, prosperity, and planetary wellbeing. Over the past decade, the hospitality and tourism industries and destination communities have emerged as powerful platforms for advancing and contesting these goals. Hospitality and tourism encompass all 17 SDGs, either directly or indirectly, from economic growth and decent work (SDG 8) to responsible consumption and production (SDG 12), climate action (SDG 13), and partnerships for the goals (SDG 17).

Appel publié par Current Issues in Tourism. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Reflecting on the First Decade (2015–2025) of SDG achievements and gaps
  • Critical reviews of how research to date references SDGs and where conceptual or methodological gaps persist
  • Evaluating tourism and hospitality's contribution to all 17 SDGs, including SDG 1 (No Poverty) and SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) through community tourism, local sourcing, and food redistribution
  • Examining progress toward SDG 3 (Good Health and Wellbeing) through wellness tourism, workplace health initiatives, and traveller safety
  • Assessing SDG 4 (Quality Education) via tourism and hospitality curriculum transformation, sustainability literacy, and lifelong learning
  • Policy coherence and alignment of tourism strategies with SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions), focusing on governance, transparency, and ethical practices
  • Reviewing the role of SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure) in sustainable destination design, transport systems, and smart tourism
  • Integrating SDG 8 (Decent Work), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), and SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) through inclusive recruitment, fair wages, and leadership opportunities
  • Advancing SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) via food waste management, circular hospitality systems, and sustainable event management
  • Strengthening SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities) by aligning urban tourism, heritage conservation, and destination capacity management
  • Building SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) through cross-sector collaborations among government, academia, and private enterprises
  • Linking SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) to energy-efficient hotel design, water conservation, and waste-water reuse
  • Exploring SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 14 (Life Below Water), and SDG 15 (Life on Land) through carbon-neutral travel, biodiversity protection, and eco-restoration tourism
  • Applying SDG 9 (Innovation and Infrastructure) and SDG 16 (Institutions) in AI-driven sustainability measurement, blockchain transparency, and smart destination governance
  • Embedding SDG 3 (Health) and SDG 11 (Communities) in wellness, resilience, and crisis recovery frameworks
  • Integrating ethical, cultural, and spiritual perspectives on sustainability to support SDG 4 (Education) and SDG 17 (Partnerships)
  • Conceptualising post-SDG paradigms such as regenerative tourism, circular hospitality, etc.
  • Examining the intersections of sustainability with digital transformation, big data, and tourism intelligence systems
  • Developing cross-SDG frameworks and metrics to capture interlinkages (e.g., SDG 8–12–13 synergies)
  • Big data analytics, AI, and social media mining for SDG progress tracking and destination reporting
  • Comparative cross-national or longitudinal studies assessing tourism's SDG impact
  • Theorising host–guest–destination dynamics as a holistic system contributing to SDG 1–17 interdependence

item.title: Sustainable Luxury Tourism: Opportunities, Tensions, and Impacts
item.content:encoded:
Kalliopi Chatzipanagiotou, University of Glasgow

Achilleas Boukis, University of Birmingham

George Christodoulides, American University of Sharjah

Raffaele Filieri, Audencia Business School

Luxury tourism is expected to grow faster than any other industry segment. Although scholarship on luxury tourism has expanded in recent years, much of this work focuses on its economic dimensions, often overlooking its broader sustainable, social and ethical implications. The relationship between sustainability and luxury tourism has received increasing attention in recent years, yet we know little about what "sustainable luxury" actually means, given the tension between exclusivity and responsible resource use. Furthermore, while many luxury tourists express concern for sustainability, there remains limited empirical evidence on how such concerns translate into actual decision-making or on the trade-offs they are willing to accept.

Appel publié par Journal of Sustainable Tourism. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Designing and conceptualizing sustainable luxury tourism experiences
  • Luxury tourism consumption practices and sustainable behaviors
  • Emerging forms of luxury tourism through a sustainability lens
  • Cultural authenticity and heritage in sustainable luxury experiences
  • Personalization, exclusivity, and sustainability tensions in luxury tourism
  • Storytelling, experience design, and sustainability communication
  • The environmental and social "dark sides" of luxury tourism
  • Local communities, inclusion, and social value creation in sustainable luxury tourism
  • Labor practices and working conditions in sustainable luxury hospitality
  • Destination branding, image, and sustainable luxury positioning
  • Stakeholder collaboration and governance in sustainable luxury tourism
  • Sustainable luxury within tourism ecosystems and power dynamics
